html_en:
Anthropic is having a big week — confessing to quality regressions, shipping enterprise infrastructure, and weaving Claude deeper into the browser — while Microsoft's Kevin Scott articulates the broader vision: we're building a new internet, this time for agents.

Anthropic Comes Clean on Claude Code Degradation

It takes intellectual honesty to publish a postmortem this candid. Anthropic's engineering blog this week detailed three separate changes that quietly degraded Claude Code quality for users over the past two months — and none of them were caught by internal evals until users complained loudly enough.

The culprits: a March 4 decision to silently drop default reasoning effort from high to medium (to reduce UI freezing), a caching bug that made Claude "forget" its own reasoning mid-session, and an April 16 verbosity-reduction prompt that broke coding quality. Because each change hit a different slice of traffic on a different schedule, the aggregate looked like "broad, inconsistent degradation" — exactly the kind of thing that's hard to pin down and easy to dismiss as user noise.

The conclusion is worth reading in full: "All three issues have now been resolved as of April 20 (v2.1.116)... As of April 23, we're resetting usage limits for all subscribers." A goodwill gesture, and a signal that Anthropic knows trust in developer tools is fragile.

As @steipete observed with characteristic economy:

"cli was a year ago. apps maybe 6 months. now it's services, web, cloud sessions."
The trajectory is clear — and the quality bar has to rise with it.

The Agentic Infrastructure Stack Takes Shape

Beyond the postmortem, Anthropic shipped two substantial pieces of infrastructure this week. The Managed Agents architecture post explains how the team decoupled the "brain" (Claude and its harness) from the "hands" (sandboxes and tools) — borrowing the classic pets-vs-cattle framing from distributed systems lore. The insight: harnesses encode assumptions about what models can't do, and those assumptions go stale as models improve. Building against stable interfaces rather than brittle implementations is the only way to keep up.

Practically, this unlocks self-hosted sandboxes and MCP tunnels — letting enterprises run Claude agents entirely within their own perimeter. Code execution, sensitive files, private APIs: none of it needs to leave your infrastructure. Partners like Cloudflare, Vercel, Daytona, and Modal handle the compute; Anthropic handles the model and session state. Early customers include Clay (GTM automation), Rogo (institutional finance), and Amplitude (design tooling).

Meanwhile, the Claude Chrome extension got a meaningful upgrade: sessions now persist across desktop, web, and mobile.

"Your Claude in Chrome sessions now carry over to desktop, web, and mobile. Conversations are saved, and your skills and connectors work in the browser." — @claudeai
Available on Max and Team plans today, Pro coming soon. One year ago, Perplexity reportedly offered to buy Chrome. Anthropic just moved in anyway.

Kevin Scott's Vision: MCP Is the New HTTP

The best framing of where all this is heading came from Microsoft CTO Kevin Scott on the AI & I podcast. Watch/Listen: Microsoft's Vision for an Internet Made for Agents.

Scott's central idea: the shift from scaling law hype to agentic infrastructure isn't a retreat — it's a maturation. Models have gotten good enough that the bottleneck is now the plumbing around them.

"I think the reasoning capabilities of the models has actually gotten a little bit ahead of what we're using the models to do in products... I've been talking a lot lately about this thing called the capability overhang." — Kevin Scott

His analogy for the protocols emerging around agents is clarifying:

"You've seen the first glimmers of real progress with simple open protocols like MCP that are serving the same purpose in this agentic web as HTTP does on the internet, and where you have things like NL web that are serving the same moral equivalent purpose as HTML does on the internet." — Kevin Scott

The memory problem gets specific attention. Agents today are "a little bit transactional" — coherent within a task, then starting from scratch. That limits how much you can delegate. Solving persistent, cross-session memory is Scott's near-term priority, and Anthropic's Claude Cowork persistence announcement looks like one answer to exactly that problem.

Cheaper Models, More Demand: Jevons Paradox Arrives

This week's model releases from DeepSeek and Grok prompted Box CEO Aaron Levie to articulate something the industry has been dancing around:

"This is truly Jevons paradox for AI playing out. By bringing down the cost of AI, demand will continue to accelerate. When I talk to enterprises, they have vastly more use-cases for what they'd like agents to handle than generally what they're able to budget for today. They want agents to scan their codebases for security issues. They want agents to review all their documents... When we bring down the cost of AI or drive up capability levels, it opens up all new use cases."

The application layer implication follows naturally. As @realmadhuguru put it:

"The biggest alpha in AI products over the next few years is in the application layer. Models will keep getting cheaper, better and more local. The differentiation will come from deeply understanding specific user workflows and having the imagination to redesign the experience around them."

On the integration front, Google's Josh Woodward announced another wave of Gemini integrations — OpenTable, Zocdoc, Ticketmaster, Otter, Wix, and more — signaling that the race to become the orchestration layer for daily tasks is very much on.

Signals & Noise

Matt Turck with the taxonomy update of the week:

"Graph engineering is the new loop engineering which is the new harness engineering which is the new context engineering which is the new prompt engineering. Hope this clarifies any confusion."

Thomas Sottiaux quietly dropped that some product (signals point to a consumer app) crossed 15 million users, with a Linux ship already in the rearview. Details sparse, excitement palpable.

Peter Yang's essay argues voice is becoming the orchestration layer for computing — with personal computers migrating to the cloud and trust emerging as the key differentiator. Worth a read if you're thinking about where the interface layer lands.

And finally, Anthropic's Amanda Askell — who thinks carefully about AI ethics for a living — reminds us that moral reasoning is genuinely hard and contextual:

"When I started playing Skyrim, I quickly realized you can make a lot of progress without doing any killing. You can also adopt orphans and build them nice houses, so I focused on that. I honestly don't really remember the plot beyond 'that challenging fantasy philanthropy game'."
Some of the best alignment intuitions come from unexpected places.
html_zh:
今天的AI世界，基础设施正在悄然重塑：从Claude的代理架构升级，到Anthropic坦诚承认的质量回退事件，AI从"聊天工具"彻底蜕变为"云端运行的基础设施"这一转型，正在加速落地。

🔧 Anthropic的公开检讨：质量下滑背后的三个Bug

AI公司少有愿意把自己的失误写成技术博客发出来的。Anthropic做到了。这篇事后复盘文章坦诚地披露了过去一个月Claude Code质量下滑的三个根因，读来令人印象深刻。

三个问题分别是：3月4日，Claude Code的默认推理强度被悄悄从"高"降至"中"以减少延迟；3月26日，一个缓存优化Bug导致Claude每轮对话都会"失忆"；4月16日，一条减少冗余输出的系统提示词与其他改动叠加，严重拖累了代码质量。由于三个问题影响的用户群体和时间段各不相同，叠加在一起看起来像是"大范围、不一致的退化"，难以定位。

"这不是用户应该从Claude Code得到的体验。截至4月23日，我们正在为所有订阅用户重置使用限额。" —— Anthropic工程博客

这种透明度在大型AI公司中并不常见。更重要的信号是：Anthropic现在将所有模型的默认推理强度调回"高"，Opus 4.7甚至默认为"xhigh"。他们明确站队了——宁可慢，不能蠢。

🏗️ "大脑"与"双手"分离：代理架构的新范式

Anthropic同天发布了两篇重量级工程文章，共同描绘了企业级AI代理的未来形态。

《Scaling Managed Agents》用了一个精妙的计算机科学类比：就像操作系统将硬件虚拟化为抽象接口（进程、文件），让上层软件不必关心底层硬件是1970年代的磁盘还是现代SSD，Managed Agents将代理的三个核心组件——会话（session）、执行框架（harness）、沙盒（sandbox）——解耦为独立接口。

"我们把这理解为'大脑'（Claude和其执行框架）与'双手'（执行动作的沙盒和工具）以及'会话记录'的解耦。每个部分都成为独立接口，对其他部分做最少的假设，并且可以独立失败或被替换。" —— Anthropic工程博客

这套架构解决了一个老问题：以前所有组件塞在一个容器里，容器一挂，会话全丢，工程师不得不"护理"（nurse）故障容器。现在容器变成了"牲畜"（cattle）——挂了就扔，新起一个，会话状态完好无损地保存在外部。

配套的新功能公告则把这套架构落地为具体产品：企业现在可以让Claude代理在自己的基础设施内执行工具调用（支持Cloudflare、Daytona、Modal、Vercel等托管沙盒提供商），并通过MCP隧道连接私有网络内的数据库和API，无需暴露任何公网端口。

🌐 代理互联网：MCP时代的"HTTP时刻"

Microsoft CTO Kevin Scott在Every的播客中描述了他对"代理互联网"的判断，与Anthropic的架构方向高度呼应。

"你已经看到了真正进展的第一缕曙光——像MCP这样简单的开放协议，在这个代理互联网中扮演着与HTTP在互联网中同样的角色；而NL Web则扮演着与HTML在互联网中同等意义的角色。你将会看到这些简单的、可组合的东西不断叠加……" —— Kevin Scott，Watch/Listen: AI & I Podcast

他还点出了当前代理的核心瓶颈：记忆。现在的代理是"事务性"的——完成一件任务后，记忆可能完全消失，下次从头开始，这严重制约了向代理委托复杂任务的能力。这与Anthropic在架构层面解决会话持久化的努力，指向同一个问题。

@steipete用一句话总结了这场演化的时间线，令人深思：

"CLI是一年前。应用程序大概是六个月前。现在是服务、Web、云端会话。" —— @steipete

📱 集成大战：Gemini扩张，Claude跨设备

平台层面的竞争也在加速。Google的Josh Woodward宣布Gemini新增一波应用集成：

"Gemini在你每天使用的应用中完成任务。从今天起，新一波集成正在推出：Angi、Fever、GetYourGuide、Granola、iHeartRadio、OpenTable、Otter、Pandora、Ticketmaster、Wix、Zocdoc、Zoho……如果你想合作，私信我。" —— @joshwoodward

Claude则在今天完成了一个关键的跨设备打通：Chrome扩展中的会话现在可以与桌面端、Web端和移动端同步，用户的技能和连接器在浏览器中同样可用。恰在一年前，@swyx提醒大家：Perplexity曾经提出收购Google Chrome——当时听起来是个玩笑，今天看来是一场浏览器入口的正面对决。

💡 散论：应用层的机会与噪音

Box CEO Aaron Levie在DeepSeek和Grok新模型发布后，写下了他对AI经济学的判断：

"这是AI领域杰文斯悖论的现实演绎。通过降低AI成本，需求将持续加速。当我与企业交谈时，他们想让代理做的事情，远远超出了他们今天能负担的预算……当我们降低AI成本或提升能力水平，就会催生全新的使用场景，进而驱动更大的需求。" —— @levie

@realmadhuguru则给出了更务实的建议：未来几年AI产品最大的Alpha在应用层，模型会越来越便宜、越来越强，差异化来自于对特定用户工作流的深刻理解，以及围绕这些工作流重新设计体验的想象力。而@mattturck以一贯的幽默戳破了术语泡沫：

"图工程（Graph engineering）是新的循环工程，循环工程是新的框架工程，框架工程是新的上下文工程，上下文工程是新的提示词工程。希望这能消除任何困惑。" —— @mattturck
